title: Erasoft / RQ progs preservation archive — scope hold
reason: Hold at the demonstrated incomplete/binary-provenance scope; no project promoted. README provides author provenance, addresses and runtime notes for several games and tools; tree contains D64/D71/ZIP images, scans and screenshots rather than textual implementations. LICENSE explicitly says there is no source code because the programs were entered in machine language via the C128 monitor. It licenses that code under Apache-2.0, other assets under CC-BY-4.0, and specifically forbids reuse of ripped TMRT music/clouds. CHANGELOG documents binary-era fixes including load addresses, C128 bank setup and modified intros. README specifies NTSC origins and a True Drive Emulation caveat for The Race. Hold for binary-preservation provenance; do not promote as a source reconstruction merely because code is licensed. Disk contents were not extracted and no substantive machine-code disassembly was independently reviewed. Original unmodified binaries and cleaned-up variants are not interchangeable; changelog lists changes. Ripped assets and third-party recracks require careful rights separation. License: Code Apache-2.0; most assets CC-BY-4.0; explicitly excludes ripped TMRT music and BC’s Quest for Tires clouds.

title: AnimPlayer — cross-platform Amiga animation viewer
reason: Approved substantive repository-level discovery. Hollywood application plays Amiga ANIM5/7/8/16/32 and YAFA plus FLIC, with playlist and GIF export features. Hollywood application plays Amiga ANIM5/7/8/16/32 and YAFA plus FLIC, with playlist and GIF export features. Classic use is practical only beyond 68060 performance with RTG, according to README; do not claim stock Amiga usability. MUI/Zune is required on Amiga-like systems. GPL-3.0 applies to application source; Hollywood and linked plugins have independent availability/licensing. AROS is explicitly supported upstream but absent from inspected canonical labels, so flagged rather than silently added. Repository metadata is not marked as a GitHub fork, but this does not erase explicit code/asset ancestry. Root-normalized dedup and prior-root screening passed the 1498-project baseline. VS Code tasks explicitly compile classic Amiga, OS4, AROS, MorphOS and several modern hosts. Build flags remain null because no sufficiently scoped present-tree success was independently established; README historical or compatibility statements remain in notes. byte_exact is null: no comparison was performed.

title: Spritemate: C64 sprite editor and snapshot tools
reason: Promoted at the demonstrated source/tool scope. Browser-hosted sprite authoring and static VICE snapshot analysis. It parses C64-specific graphics/machine-state data, but does not execute 6502 instructions or reconstruct a historical game. No CPU architecture is assigned from TypeScript or the formats. Rights: Complete root MIT license. Example/extracted game graphics require separate rights review. All build facts remain null; source and overall audit states remain partial.

title: Amiga Games — Dot Chase, Fractalus and Void Trader collection
reason: Approved Amiga-game discovery. amiga_games is one source-available AmigaBridge game collection with its own canonical root, distinct from the already-tracked parent tooling. Three inspected anchors establish the bounded game collection: Dot Chase implements maze dot-eating, ghost states, power pellets, fruit, score, lives and level completion; Fractalus implements terrain flight, pilot rescue/deception, landing/airlock/takeoff, combat, fuel/shield win/loss and attract mode; Void Trader implements space combat, docking, station trading, cargo/credits, salvage and win/game-over states. Void Trader prices are fixed with 90% resale; variable-price trade routes remain future work. The complete 426-entry tree was inspected and three game anchors were read in depth; this is not a claim that every listed game or asset was audited. The three per-game Makefiles require the external parent AmigaBridge headers and libbridge.a at ../../amiga-bridge, so the game repository alone is insufficient without that layout, dependency and matching compiler/library architecture. Classic builds use -noixemul; the two PPC branches use newlib and architecture-specific audio stubs. Fractalus/Void Trader treat failed ab_init as optional at runtime, so a running host MCP/daemon is not established as universally required merely by README deployment instructions. Dot Chase ignores that return value; daemon-free execution remains unverified. Parent examples-pin mismatch is retained under relationships. No collection build, binary availability or playthrough was independently verified; all four build flags remain null.

title: Amiga Enforcer — original MMU memory-debugging suite
reason: Michael Sinz's original Enforcer source snapshot, including MMU handlers, SegTracker, FindHit, LawBreaker and MMU utilities. title: PCQ Pascal — author's original Amiga compiler archive
reason: Approved substantive repository-level discovery. Author release of original PCQ code, not a decompilation or same-lineage mirror. No standard license file. Author readme.md expressly permits use and explains he did not remove historical shareware/copyright restrictions; ReadMe.txt still says registered-disk files must not be distributed. Preserve the tension rather than label MIT/public domain. Compiler source and runtime code are present; historic disks include third-party tools/docs with separate provenance and terms. Native classic Amiga/m68k compiler; precise minimum CPU and RAM not verified. GitHub's automated OpenEdge ABL language label is incorrect for the inspected Pascal source. Source-only review; all build flags and AI usage remain unknown.

title: VirusExecutor — preserved Amiga antivirus source
reason: Jan Erik Olausen's VirusExecutor C/assembly source preserved under GPLv3. Approved as one substantive original-source/native-tool/homebrew record after exact-root screening. Build/equivalence remain unverified; licensing and completeness caveats are retained.

title: Battleship — native AmigaOS 3 game source
reason: Approved games-only publication. This distinct native AmigaOS 3 C implementation has full, light and own-screen Battleship variants. The reviewed complete own-screen source implements ship placement/rotation/undo, player and computer shooting, hit counts, new game and terminal win/loss states; packaged LhA files and artwork are also present. The project is counted once across these variants. Its canonical tickBit/Amiga-Battleship root and subject-code identity do not match prior-reviewed roots or a current catalogue record. README requires VBCC with -c99 and says its backfill-hook implementation prevents direct use of other compilers. The checked-in source provides the own-screen compile line with -fpu=68881. C files and packed LhA binary distributions exist, but their correspondence and a clean rebuild were not tested. The README warns resource/library/allocation failures may behave badly. These are documented build/source facts, not observed compilation or playability; all four build flags remain null.

title: mpw-emu — experimental PowerPC MPW tool runner
reason: Approved source-reviewed original-binary runner discovery. src/main.rs reads the requested original tool through MacFile, parses its PEF data fork and resources, links it into emulated memory, forwards argv and returns the emulated exit status. README reports MWCPPC from CodeWarrior Pro 1 and DeRez results. These are upstream demonstrations, not independent compatibility tests; this record is the experimental runner rather than CodeWarrior/MPW itself. Root and record ID are absent from the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and the prior dedup index. Inspected main tip: a0d23d515987ae5b486da9430e0b78a02ac93b4f. Substantive emulator/development tooling: src/linker.rs builds transition-vector shims for imported symbols; src/emulator/mod.rs installs InterfaceLib/StdCLib and Toolbox/C-library callbacks and handles them through a PowerPC supervisor-call hook. Original PEF instructions run inside Unicorn without booting Classic Mac OS. Missing imports remain logged, the initialization vector is explicitly unimplemented, and the README lists missing PEF relocations and APIs. XCOFF support is not established. The complete 37-entry tree has no LICENSE/COPYING grant, Cargo.toml has no license field, and repository metadata reports license null. Do not describe it as permissively licensed or assume public source authorizes redistribution. Unicorn and Rust dependencies retain their separate terms, as do original CodeWarrior/MPW executables and libraries. README’s comparison with SheepShaver/QEMU describes the purpose; no fork relationship is established. Merged PR #1 concerns Retro68-produced MacBinary II input and is not evidence that Retro68 is this runner’s implementation or guest CPU. Overall source/author/dependency graph coverage remains partial.

title: Rubicon — disk protection reconstruction
reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Disk-protection analysis and native protection-track writer/copier for Rubicon. README reports successfully producing a master disk using WP/RUBICOPY and the explanation describes the physical-drive result. Runnable=true is an upstream-only disk-tool claim; no drive writes, assembler build, gameplay or independent comparison were performed. The perfect-master statement does not establish byte_exact. Zibri/RamJam documents new protection-track reconstruction for the existing Rubicon game. The distributed D64 images and game data remain distinct from the new writer code; no repository license grant was found.

title: BassoonTracker

title: talkip

title: Grizzards

title: Earth Shaker

title: vaelen/clarus

title: TheFakeMontyOnTheRun/space-trashman-blues

title: Sargon III — Apple II commented disassembly
reason: Distinct substantive game research root after programmatic catalogue/decision-root screening and primary source/lineage review.

title: Sargon III Oric binary-patch port
reason: Related port explicitly patches the Apple II game binary studied by Oric4ever/sargon3_disassembly, adding Oric graphics and tape packaging. title: SimCoupe
reason: Canonical repository is already represented by SimCoupe — SAM Coupé emulator.

title: tony-cruise/colecovision-games-source umbrella

title: tom-seddon/basic_editor

title: Mehmood Spectrum compiler — incomplete type-in preservation

title: fuseadf — Amiga image filesystem bridge

title: Game Boy APU behavioural test ROM

title: Theme Park DOS resource viewer
reason: Views/extracts Theme Park floppy/CD sprites, palettes, animation and sound resources. Music playback is explicitly experimental.

title: DiztinGUIsh — trace-assisted SNES disassembler
reason: Combines SNES ROM mapping, labels and emulator trace/CDL information including 65816 register-width context. Importer respects the selected mapping rather than retaining inconsistent detected offsets.

title: Space Cadet Pinball — Nintendo DS port
reason: Native DS/DSi adaptation of the reverse-engineered Space Cadet engine. Full Tilt CADET data is reported nonworking, and DS downscaling/light issues differ from DSi.

title: dcc — DOS executable decompiler continuation
reason: Historical DOS-to-C decompiler substantially reworked with a Qt frontend and MZ/PSP loading. Memory models, arrays and recovery remain constrained; historical binaries do not establish that current source builds.

title: AProSys — historical Amiga music tracker sources
reason: Historical tracker source archive with two differently aged source trees. Author cannot confidently identify the final version; src-q/ad.c explicitly is not the version used in AProSys.

title: AppleIIDev — Merlin32 development workflow
reason: Source examples and reusable graphics routines with Node/VSCode tasks that assemble, replace files in a disk image and launch AppleWin. This is a development workflow, not a new assembler or game reconstruction.

title: mkd64 — modular C64 disk-image builder
reason: Core track/sector writer with CBM DOS directory, extra-track and separator modules; supports per-file placement/interleave. Unknown options can be silently ignored because modules interpret them.

title: lyxass — Lynx and Jaguar macro assembler
reason: Macro assembler includes native Jaguar GPU/DSP instruction encoding and Lynx support. Include search uses BLL_ROOT versus BJL_ROOT for different targets.

title: texconv — Dreamcast texture creation

title: VPW Studio — N64 wrestling-game editing suite

title: Game Boy Tetris — C reconstruction targeting GBA

title: BBC Lisp-derived interpreter and compiler

title: Extermination — PS2 matching reconstruction

title: Acorn BBC BASIC 128 source restoration

title: clown68000 CPU and disassembler library

title: AlexLib RISC OS source library

title: 86-DOS disk-image reconstruction tools

title: Amiga MC68060 support package
reason: Historical Motorola integer/floating-point support plus Amiga 68060.library integration and exception-vector setup. Distinguish vendor core from Amiga callouts; not 68000-compatible library and no system vectors changed or binaries executed here.

title: CP/M 2.2 CCP and BDOS source
reason: Reformatted original CCP/BDOS for Macro Assembler AS. Upstream exactness claim explicitly excludes six-byte serial numbers in each component; not complete machine-specific BIOS or an unconditional byte-exact whole operating system image.

title: RAMbrandt Atari source archive
reason: Author-supplied Forth graphics program, Okimate utilities and multiple dated disk/source variants. Two archived images have documented bad sectors; latest source must not imply all historical variants are complete or repaired.

title: FileCore Mountin filesystem continuation
reason: RISC OS FileCore source with independently maintained Mountin contributions, defaulting to fixed-media/old-directory feature branch. Preserve original FileCore lineage and branch identity; concrete workspace/cache code is not proof every filesystem variant is supported.

title: Ghidra NES ROM analysis extension
reason: iNES import, NES memory map, labels and 6502 language integration. Explicit mapper scope is NROM/0; tested Ghidra 10.0.3 does not establish current-version compatibility or automated recovery of complete source.

title: X68000 ADPCM helper library
reason: Header-only IOCS wrappers and recorder/player examples with rate/output modes and busy polling. Nonblocking calls require caller buffer lifetime and completion handling; this is hardware access glue, not a software ADPCM codec.

title: MSX REA media analysis toolkit
reason: ROM/DISK triage, mapper heuristics and evidence-report pipeline exposed through CLI/MCP. Bank-write counts are explicitly heuristic, not mapper proof; LLM client integration is capability, not evidence the project was AI-authored.

title: Acorn NFS 3.34 disassembly
reason: Generated assembly plus Py8Dis annotation program labels Econet/NFS routines, registers and mixed data. Specific 8 KiB ROM version; tooling source is reproducible annotation evidence, not independent source recovery of every NFS release.

title: um80 MACRO-80 compatible toolchain
reason: Assembler, linker, librarian, cross-reference, disassembler and syntax translator. REL-format implementation documents Microsoft versus DRI differences and extended symbols; compatible subset and extensions must not be conflated with unrestricted original-tool equivalence.

title: ApplEm
reason: Primary README documents Apple II/IIgs emulation with built-in CPU debugger, memory inspection, disk exploration/disassembly and agent control.

title: AZAS / MINI-DOS historical development system
reason: Preserved Z80 development system with bootable images and Z80-to-8086 conversion tooling.

title: Chiller 2 — Commodore 64 homebrew platform game
reason: Andy Vaisey/Cosine's source-available 2020 C64 platform game with twelve levels, playable boy/girl characters and PAL/NTSC handling. readme.txt documents controls, gameplay and named playtesters. ACME assembly source specifies PRG output and exomizer packaging; D64/TAP releases are present.

title: CP/M for OS X — native macOS CP/M-80 runtime
reason: Primary documentation establishes an integrated Z80 emulator and CP/M-80 reimplementation for macOS.

title: Desolate — TI-83 Plus to ZX Spectrum native port
reason: Released native Spectrum port of Patrick Prendergast/tr1p1ea's TI-83 Plus Desolate. Repository includes original-game SkoolKit control annotations and memory-dump disassembly commands alongside adapted Z80 gameplay. The build assembles with Pasmo/SjASMPlus, compresses with LZSA and produces TAP/TZX. README links walkthroughs and related Vector-06c/UKNC ports.

title: Ghidra Sega Saturn Loader
reason: Primary documentation establishes concrete Saturn ISO/save-state loading, SH-2 state mapping and Ghidra build/install support.

title: ep128-devel
reason: Enterprise 128 crt0, library and C wrappers for SDCC's Z80 backend.

title: mz800emu — Sharp MZ-800/700/1500 emulator and debugger
reason: Primary documentation establishes a current multi-model emulator with integrated Z80 debugging, profiling and MCP analysis controls.

title: Jaguar Cartridge Reader
reason: Preservation firmware that dumps Jaguar cartridges and adds a non-destructive cartridge-bus analyzer plus evidence-based 16-bit read modes for newer cartridge layouts.

title: Midwinter — DOS behavioral decode and terrain reconstruction
reason: Documented analysis of DOS MIDWINTR.EXE plus concrete Python terrain/world reconstruction, EXEPACK analysis and sprite-extraction code. Includes function/evidence ledger rather than playable game. Original Midwinter platform history must not mislabel inspected target as ST. No runnable game or source-rebuild claim. Author's 602-function coverage and bit-equality claims are upstream; source notes interior/border, tree-lattice and building-pad limitations. ~20 items await runtime review. User supplies original assets. Separate closed UE5 remaster is not this repository. Upstream reports operational asset extraction and terrain replicas with bounded runtime comparisons. This repository explicitly contains no playable game or recompilable whole-game source. Broad 602-function/bit-equality claims are upstream and scope-limited; no independent run.

title: Street Rod — native VGA SDL3 reconstruction
reason: Native C reconstruction of the full VGA game with optional Street Rod SE car data. Maintains original data/memory structure, adds a launcher, and requires original assets; alternate graphics adapters remain unported. Reviewed on 2026-10-05; build/playability claims are upstream reports, not independent execution. Evidence: https://github.com/kylofon/street-rod-sdl3/blob/master/README.md https://github.com/kylofon/street-rod-sdl3/blob/master/srport/PORTING.md https://github.com/kylofon/street-rod-sdl3/blob/master/srport/src/game/flow_main.c https://github.com/kylofon/street-rod-sdl3/commit/0e5598e4fb45735b7c611a41b3595c91f16c3fa8 Published build: https://github.com/kylofon/street-rod-sdl3/releases/tag/v0.1.0

title: wav2cas — MSX cassette audio and CAS toolkit
reason: Implemented cassette converter/synthesizer with embedded tests Pure-Python FSK demodulation and CAS encoding, with adaptive timing/confidence handling and optional ffmpeg conversion; adjacent scripts generate cassette audio and model recording/playback effects. Reviewed decode(), write_cas(), CAS synthesis and cassette DSP implementation; synthetic regression tests are present in source but were not run. This is a distinct MSX audio/CAS tool, rather than another copy of the already tracked PC-88 dwimsy tool. MSX-like is a format claim, not verified support for every retro computer. Default input conversion may use ffmpeg; pure-Python FLAC fallback is documented as slow. Root LICENSE is MIT, while cas2wav.py carries a separate public-domain assertion tied to its AI generation. Record the mixed notices without endorsing the claim that AI authorship automatically resolves rights. Tests and accuracy are upstream assertions/source facilities; no audio recovery or physical cassette test performed.

title: ckwin
reason: Historical Windows/OS/2 Kermit terminal and file-transfer application source; this candidate documents an application continuation without a specific recovery or retro development tool contribution.

title: Mars Patrol — creator-restored C64 Moon Patrol conversion
reason: Creator documents recovery of his unfinished 1985 C64 Moon Patrol conversion by disassembling and reassembling the old binary in 2024, then implementing substantial missing gameplay. Published PRG/D64 outputs and explicit PAL VICE play testing support a concrete restoration even though recovered source files are not published.

title: c64 — C64 Ultimate command-line and disk tools
reason: Concrete TypeScript CLI provides C64 Ultimate program/media deployment, scripted machine control, PETSCII keyboard input, and implemented D64 directory parsing/creation/renaming. These are directly relevant retro-development and disk-image tools at coherent repository scope.

title: vaspervnp/projectkaptara
reason: Only CPC setup/title/display and an empty gameplay self-jump are implemented. Retain the inspected evidence as a lead, not a native-game candidate. This applies the same threshold as Conquest.

title: ActionReplayAmiga
reason: Reverse engineered Action Replay hardware schematics and PAL/FPGA plans; hardware analysis rather than software or firmware reconstruction for the catalogue.

title: nitecrwl
reason: Author labels the Atari ST game decompiled; gameplay C++, GEM AES/VDI code and cross-build Makefile substantiate source recovery. Original binary identity, matching and runtime verification remain unknown.

title: ST Floormat
reason: README identifies the original source and an old source version of the group’s own demo; the Falcon hardware requirement is not evidence of reverse engineering.

title: Amiga-SpinningCube
reason: Original Amiga graphics demonstration; reviewed README/source contains no recovered legacy software or analysis-tool implementation.

title: sine_mora_tools
reason: Sine Mora BIN archive extraction/hash utilities; no identified legacy-platform reconstruction target in reviewed documentation.
